newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate down, baht firmer late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate down, baht firmer late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate fell to 8.00 percent percent in late trade on Thursday from 9.00-9.50 earlier amid high money supply in the system, dealers said.

The liquidity was expected to be tighter tomorrow due to heavy forward dollar buying in the afternoon triggered by rumours that Thailand's long-term debt ratings may face possible downgrades by Standard & Poor's Corp and Moody's Investors Service, dealers said.
Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda on Thursday refuted the rumour.
"Heavy buying of the forward dollar will make the liquidity tighter tomorrow. The coming reserve requirement will also squeeze the money supply," one dealer at a foreign said.
The baht firmed to 25.430-25.435 to the dollar late from 25.441-25.444 in early morning trade on dollar's fall abroad, dealers said.

The one-month dollar/baht swap premium rose to 8.50/9.00 satangs per dollar late compared with 7.00/8.00 earlier due to heavy offshore buying of forward dollar sparked by rumour of Thai possible rating downgrade, dealers said.
"There was heavy bidding for forward dollar from Singapore in the afternoon due to the rumour. This pushed the swap premium up," said another dealer.
The mid-rate was fixed at 25.45 to the dollar against 25.43 on Wednesday. The mid-rate of 25.45 was the lowest level since February 10, 1994.
